title: Inflation rises to 4.82 percent and wholesale prices near 10 percent as Brent hits 108 dollars before the Fed
standfirst: With Indian markets shut for Ganesh Chaturthi, the day belonged to data: retail inflation rose to 4.82 percent in August from 4.45 percent on food prices, wholesale inflation hit 9.92 percent led by fuel, and RBI Governor Malhotra met the finance minister ahead of the October 5-7 policy meeting. Brent climbed above 108 dollars as the Saudi pipeline outage kept supply tight, foreign investors have sold Rs 14,475 crore of Indian shares this month, and gold fell as traders priced an 89 percent chance of a Fed hike on Wednesday. Global tech slid after AI leaders called for a slowdown, with Nasdaq futures down nearly 2 percent and European tech at a six-week low, while ECB officials signalled more hikes and Tata Sons' chairman faces a Thursday board meeting on the RBI's listing order.

items.text: Dalal Street was closed for the holiday and reopens Tuesday, also weekly expiry, with the Nifty at 23,398.10 and the Sensex at 74,781.76. Analysts say the index is oversold and could rebound, with HDFC Bank and IT stocks the swing factors, and BofA Securities turned bullish for the first time in two years with a 26,200 Nifty target for December.
Foreign investors have sold Indian shares worth Rs 14,475 crore in September as oil and global bond yields surged, and analysts warn a US 10-year yield above 5 percent could deepen the selloff.

Brent rose 3.3 percent to 108.07 dollars even as the US said it is clearing Hormuz traffic, with the Saudi pipeline shutdown keeping supply tight. Asian shares fell, the Nikkei lost 0.8 percent and the Euro Stoxx 50 0.9 percent as European tech hit a six-week low.

Nasdaq futures tumbled nearly 2 percent after OpenAI and Anthropic leaders urged slower AI development, with Citigroup warning that an AI pause could pull the rug from under earnings revisions that have driven this year's rally.
Gold fell 0.7 percent to about 4,336 dollars as traders priced an 89 percent chance of a Fed hike, the dollar held steady with the yen near a seven-month high, and Bitcoin held near 77,700 dollars.

Retail inflation rose to 4.82 percent in August from 4.45 percent in July, marginally above forecasts, with food inflation at 5.95 percent and rural inflation at 5.23 percent. Bloomberg says it narrows the RBI's room to pause, and Governor Malhotra met the finance minister ahead of the October 5-7 policy meeting.

Wholesale inflation climbed to 9.92 percent in August, the second highest in the new series, driven by fuel and power, food and manufactured goods, and analysts warn next month may be worse as input costs are passed on.

The RBI is pulling about Rs 1 lakh crore out of the banking system through bond sales after its forex swap scheme flooded banks with cash, and it proposed a 60-day cap on account holds in cyber fraud cases with only the disputed amount frozen.

Tata Sons chairman Noel Tata faces the biggest crisis of his tenure as the RBI's listing order splits the Tata Trusts ahead of Thursday's board meeting, while legal experts see limited grounds to challenge the regulator in court.

SEBI's proposed closing auction fixes drew criticism as a hasty retreat from a reform meant to curb manipulation, though Jefferies says they remove uncertainty. Solar Industries agreed to buy South Africa's Omnia for Rs 12,951 crore, Rayzon Solar halved its IPO, and rice prices have risen 15 to 25 percent on war-driven export demand.

Reuters says the table is set for a Fed hike on Wednesday, the first under chair Warsh, with Goldman Sachs and JP Morgan both now expecting a 25 basis point move as inflation lingers. Bond investors are pushing for hikes even though they will not lower fuel prices, and the 10-year yield sits at the doorstep of 5 percent.
ECB policymakers Kazaks and Schnabel signalled more hikes may be needed as fuel and gas costs feed inflation, and the Bank of Japan is seen likely to hike this week, supporting the yen.

AI bosses are clashing with Wall Street and the White House over safety after calling for a slowdown, Anthropic picked Nasdaq for its planned IPO, and SoftBank shares tumbled 14 percent in the tech selloff.

Germany will lobby the EU for a new China policy that may include more tariffs, some companies that left China to dodge tariffs are heading back, and Trump confirmed he will scrap tariffs on Irish whiskey.

watch: Tuesday's reopening and weekly expiry on Dalal Street, with the Nifty at 23,398, HDFC Bank and IT in focus, and the 23,900 to 24,000 zone as resistance.
The Fed's decision on Wednesday, with an 89 percent chance of a quarter-point hike priced in, followed by the Bank of Japan and Bank of England.
Brent at 108 dollars and whether the Saudi East-West pipeline and Hormuz traffic recover, the key input for the rupee and India's inflation.
Thursday's Tata Sons board meeting on the RBI listing order and the opening of the NSE IPO, with the RBI's October 5-7 policy meeting now the focus after hot inflation data.
